status_definitions.OPEN: Two or more readings are supported; not decided. Later phases carry it as a switch or policy.
status_definitions.RESOLVED_BY_TEXT: The contract's own words settle it; the preferred reading is recorded with HIGH confidence.
status_definitions.EVIDENCE_NOT_PROVIDED: The contract depends on evidence the task data does not supply.
status_definitions.NOTED: An inconsistency with no effect on any charge.

confidence_definitions.MEDIUM: the text favours one reading but a stated provision points the other way
confidence_definitions.none: confidence is null where no reading is preferred

method: Readings were formed from the contract package only. Invoice, line and report data were not used to prefer any reading.

ambiguities.title: Rank of material not listed in Clause 2
ambiguities.issue: Clause 2 lists the Agreement, Parts I-VII, Schedules 1-6 and Appendices A-C, and ranks only Schedules over Parts and Part VI over Parts I-V. Part VIII, Part IX, Schedules 2C, 2D, 7 and 8, Appendices D-G and the Schedule of Variations are bound into the package but are absent from both the Contents and Clause 2 (verified on p.2 and p.3). No clause ranks them, and Clause 2 gives no rank to Appendices A-C either. Conflicts that depend on this: AMB-02, AMB-03, AMB-04, AMB-05, AMB-06, AMB-14, AMB-15, AMB-21.

readings.reading: The unlisted documents form part of the contract but have no stated rank; each conflict must be resolved on its own terms (specific over general, or kept as a sensitivity switch).

Schedule 6 states the same values ... and Schedule 2D governs.

readings.reading: Rank by name: Schedules 2C, 2D, 7 and 8 are Schedules and prevail over any Part (Clause 2); Part IX, being 'Particular Conditions (Second Series)', ranks with Part VI and prevails over Parts I-V.

evidence.source_text: A Schedule prevails over a Part, and Part VI prevails over Parts I to V.
